title: Security hardening for SIEM audit export: credential encryption, RBAC gates, and audit logging of config changes
creator: Marcus Lin
description:
Goal: deliver baseline security controls required for SIEM-ready audit export beta across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

This ticket covers three areas:
1) Credential handling/encryption for export destinations (Splunk HEC token, Datadog API key, S3 access via role/keys, KMS settings).
2) RBAC/permissions: only authorized users can create/update/delete/enable/disable/test/replay export destinations and view destination secrets.
3) Audit logging of export configuration changes: config CRUD + state changes must emit Audit Event v1 entries suitable for compliance evidence and incident investigations.

Context / why now
- Beta will be used by regulated customers; misconfigured destinations and over-permissive access are the primary risk.
- We need a clear security posture for customer security questionnaires (who can configure exports; how secrets are stored; what is logged).

In scope
A) Secrets storage + encryption
- Store destination credentials in the centralized secrets store (same primitive used for API keys / OAuth tokens) with envelope encryption.
- Ensure per-tenant key scoping: secrets must be logically isolated by workspace/tenant; include environment dimension (prod/staging) where applicable.
- Support KMS key selection policy:
  - Hosted/Dedicated: Redwood-managed KMS (default) with per-environment key separation.
  - Private: customer-managed KMS integration (where supported) OR customer-managed secret backend (per Private installer guidance).
- Never persist credentials in plaintext in control-plane DB, logs, traces, or metrics.
- Console/API behavior:
  - Secret values write-only; read endpoints return redacted placeholders.
  - Rotation: update secret without recreating destination; worker should pick up new value within bounded time.

B) RBAC model and enforcement
- Introduce new permission(s) for audit export management. Proposed:
  - audit_exports:read (view destinations, health, filters)
  - audit_exports:write (create/update/delete destination, filters)
  - audit_exports:operate (enable/disable, send test event, replay window)
- Ensure API enforces permissions on all relevant endpoints (control plane + console backend).
- Console UI should hide entrypoints for users lacking read permission, and show explicit error messaging for 403s.
- Ensure "test delivery" and "replay" are restricted to operate permission (these can generate data egress).

C) Audit logging of export config changes
- Emit Audit Event v1 events for:
  - audit_export.destination.created
  - audit_export.destination.updated
  - audit_export.destination.deleted
  - audit_export.destination.enabled / audit_export.destination.disabled / audit_export.destination.paused (if applicable)
  - audit_export.destination.test_sent (include sink type and destination id; do not include secret)
  - audit_export.destination.replay_requested (time window, destination id, safeguard confirmation)
- Include required SIEM correlation fields per schema v1: actor.*, workspace_id/tenant_id, environment, request_id, target (destination id), ip, user_agent (when present), and outcome (success/denied).
- Ensure audit records are written even on denied attempts (RBAC denied) with outcome=denied.

Non-goals
- Full customer-managed field mappings beyond schema v1.
- Exactly-once delivery semantics.
- Additional sinks beyond Splunk/Datadog/S3.

Acceptance criteria
1) Secrets
- [ ] Destination secrets are stored only in secrets store; DB contains only secret reference IDs.
- [ ] Any API response never returns secret material; logs/traces redacted.
- [ ] Rotation works: updating credentials causes worker to use new secret within <= 5 minutes (config propagation bound).
- [ ] Private install path documented for secret backend/KMS integration (handoff to ENG-13935 docs if needed).

2) RBAC
- [ ] New permissions wired into authz layer; endpoints protected.
- [ ] Console actions return 403 with consistent error code when not permitted.
- [ ] Existing roles mapped (at minimum: Workspace Admin gets write+operate; Security Admin gets read+write+operate; Viewer gets read only).

3) Audit logging
- [ ] Config changes and denied attempts generate Audit Event v1 entries.
- [ ] Events include destination id + sink type, filter summary, and relevant state changes.
- [ ] No secrets appear in audit payloads.

Implementation notes / decisions
- Use the shared secret envelope encryption service ("secrets-store") with tenant-scoped namespaces. Store reference in audit-export destination model.
- Use allowlisted structured logging fields for config payloads; redact "headers", "token", "api_key", "secret_access_key" fields by key name and by destination type.
- For audit events, store a minimal diff-like summary (e.g., changed fields list) rather than full pre/post config blobs.

Testing
- Unit tests: redaction, RBAC policy matrix, audit event emission on success/deny.
- Integration tests: create destination -> ensure DB has no secret; logs have no secret; audit stream receives expected event.
- Regression: ensure existing audit logging pipeline doesn’t create recursive export events (exporting audit-export audit events is OK; but avoid infinite loops).

Rollout
- Behind existing SIEM export feature flag (per-tenant) and additional server-side guard: deny creation unless tenant is allowlisted for beta.
- Security sign-off required before enabling beta customers.

Links
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/siem-ready-audit-export-beta-prd.json
- Schema v1: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-event-schema-v1.json
- Service doc: sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/audit-export-service.json
- Relevant PRs (expected):
  - redwood control plane: RBAC + audit log emission
  - audit-log-exporter: config redaction + secret reference usage

Open questions
- For Private deployments: do we support customer-provided KMS for envelope encryption in v1, or require external secret backend only?
- Role mapping: do we introduce a dedicated "Security Admin" role for enterprise tenants as part of this beta, or map to existing admin roles only?

Owner notes
- Security Eng (Marcus/Kevin) to review audit event names + payload fields.
- SRE to confirm audit log volume impact and whether denied attempts will create noisy patterns for large orgs.
